matchHints.exact: Ad shows only for this query and close variants (plurals, typos). For proven keywords.
matchHints.broad: Apple expands to related queries and synonyms. Cheaper, for learning how people really phrase it. Always in its own campaign.

ads.matchRule: Defend, Accelerate and Niche go as Exact into the “Habitly - Exact” campaign (you pay for that query only). Test keywords go as Broad into “Habitly - Discovery” with a low bid, together with Search Match. Every Exact keyword is added to Discovery as a Negative Exact so Broad cannot steal the proven queries. The CSV already contains both.

data.q: Where does the data come from?
data.a: From the public App Store and Google Play search and public reviews, the same results your users see, in each country you choose. For your site: your own pages, PageSpeed and your Search Console; for AI: the assistants’ real answers.

access.q: Do you need access to my accounts?
access.a: No. For an app its store name or link is enough, for a site its address. No SDK, no access to App Store Connect or the Play Console. Search Console is optional and read-only.

when.a: Every morning at 05:10 UTC, plus whenever you press “Measure ranks”. The briefing is ready when you open the app.

where.a: 30 countries on the App Store and Google Play, including the US, UK, Germany, France, Japan, Brazil and India. Each keyword is tracked per country.

ai.q: What does the AI do, exactly?
ai.a: It proposes titles, subtitles and keyword-field wording based on your ranks and competitors, and explains each suggestion. It never changes your listing; you decide.

apps.q: Can I track more than one project?
apps.a: Yes. Every app or website gets its own workspace with its own keywords, competitors and settings, and you switch between them from the left rail. A website can take its app later.

lab.a: A listing change you log in Seenlab (new title, subtitle or keyword field). Seenlab compares your ranks in the 7 days before with up to 14 days after, leaving out the first 2 days while Apple reindexes, and shows the effect per keyword.

lab.title: Every change is an experiment.
lab.body: Change a title or subtitle and Seenlab treats it like an experiment: it compares the 7 days before with up to 14 days after, skips the 2 days Apple needs to reindex, and shows the effect keyword by keyword.

discount.q: Student, open source or just starting out?

gsc.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect Search Console? Its numbers are removed from Seenlab.

gsc.noDataSub: Google’s data arrives with a 2–3 day delay. If this stays empty, check that the right property is picked.

gsc.noOpportunities: No searches between positions 4 and 20 with enough impressions yet.

audit.never: Your site hasn’t been checked yet.
audit.neverSub: The crawler reads your pages the way Google and AI crawlers do, without running JavaScript, and lists what stands in the way. It takes about a minute.
audit.speedSub: Google PageSpeed Insights for the home page.
audit.speedQuota: PageSpeed’s free daily quota is used up — the next audit tries again.
audit.speedQuotaAdmin: PageSpeed’s shared daily quota is used up. Set GOOGLE_PSI_KEY (a free Google API key) in the server’s .env for your own quota.

unreachable.title: Page didn’t load
unreachable.fix: The server didn’t answer in time. Check that the page is online and not blocking unknown visitors.

not_found.title: Broken page (4xx)
not_found.fix: Linked pages that return “not found” waste crawl time and lose visitors. Fix the page or remove the links to it.

server_error.title: Server error (5xx)
server_error.fix: Google drops pages that keep failing. Check the server logs for these URLs.

broken_links.title: Links to broken pages
broken_links.fix: These pages link to URLs that don’t work. Update or remove the links.

title_missing.title: Missing title
title_missing.fix: The title is what Google shows as the blue link. Give every page a unique title with its main keyword.

title_long.title: Title too long
title_long.fix: Google cuts titles at about 60 characters. Put the important words first.

title_short.title: Title too short
title_short.fix: A few words don’t say what the page is about. Aim for 30–60 characters.

title_duplicate.title: Same title on several pages
title_duplicate.fix: Google can’t tell these pages apart. Give each one its own title.

description_missing.title: Missing meta description
description_missing.fix: Without one, Google picks a random snippet. Write 1–2 sentences that make people click.

description_long.title: Meta description too long
description_long.fix: Anything over about 160 characters gets cut.

description_short.title: Meta description too short
description_short.fix: Use the space: say what the page offers and why it’s worth a click.

h1_missing.title: No main heading (H1)
h1_missing.fix: Every page needs one clear H1 that says what it’s about.

h1_multiple.title: Several H1 headings
h1_multiple.fix: Keep one H1 per page and use H2 for sections.

noindex.title: Hidden from Google (noindex)
noindex.fix: These pages ask search engines not to list them. Fine for private pages, a problem for anything you want found.

js_only.title: Empty without JavaScript
js_only.fix: Crawlers that don’t run JavaScript — including most AI crawlers — see a blank page. Prerender or server-render these pages.

thin_content.title: Very little text
thin_content.fix: Pages with under 200 words rarely rank. Explain more: features, use cases, answers to common questions.

canonical_missing.title: No canonical link
canonical_missing.fix: Tell Google which URL is the main one, so duplicates (with ?ref=…, trailing slashes) don’t compete.

images_no_alt.title: Images without alt text
images_no_alt.fix: Alt text helps image search, accessibility and AI assistants that read your page.

slow.title: Slow response
slow.fix: The server took over 2.5 seconds to answer. Speed affects ranking and conversions.

viewport_missing.title: Not set up for mobile
viewport_missing.fix: Add a viewport meta tag, otherwise Google treats the page as not mobile-friendly.

og_missing.title: No share preview (Open Graph)
og_missing.fix: Links shared on social apps and chats show no title or image.

lang_missing.title: No language set
lang_missing.fix: Add lang to the html tag so search engines know who the page is for.
